tasks.task: Write a 60 to 90 second explainer script

items.when: Before the script, to plan which picture pairs with each idea so the point sticks
When product notes must become a timed script: what we hear beside what we see
When the approach is open, to get four different kinds of script, each with its opening
When the product is best shown working from the inside, to try a how-it-works version
When the script uses the product's own jargon and a newcomer would not follow it
When the script is drafted, to find every line that trips when spoken and fix it
Before sign-off, to check the script fits the length and what to cut if not

tasks.task: Fit a script to a fixed length

items.when: When a script must fit 30, 60 or 90 seconds and you need to know what to cut
When the script is a little long and must lose words without losing the point
When you must choose which lines to drop, to find the weak ones first
After the cut, to check the shorter lines still read well aloud

tasks.task: Write a product demo walkthrough script

items.when: When each screen or step needs its spoken line beside what the viewer sees
When the demo should let the viewer see the result first, to compare that order
When you have screenshots or a page and want a short demo video or GIF made
When the walkthrough can be narrated slides made from a written document
Before recording, to fix lines that are hard to say while clicking through the product

tasks.task: Storyboard a live-action video

items.when: Before the shots, to find the one idea, feeling and symbol the opening should carry
When an approved script must become a timed shot table and a shoot plan
When you want a second pass of timed shots from the script to compare coverage
When the board is talking heads, to decide what viewers know and plan the visual beats
When the board is drafted, to check it still makes sense with the sound off
When the pictures only repeat the voice-over, to test what they say on their own

tasks.task: Storyboard an animated explainer and brief the animator

items.when: When the script is approved and each scene needs its motion, text and audio in a table
When the animator needs an exact build plan and a table of every on-screen word
When a 3D look is an option, to see a storyboard with image and clip prompts
When a hand-made cutout look is an option, to compare it with the clean version
When scenes jump and the viewer cannot follow what happened between two frames
Before the brief goes out, to check the visuals carry the message without sound

tasks.task: Storyboard a short vertical video

items.when: When the format is open, to pick one and get a script outline and ten hooks
When the first two seconds are undecided, to get ten hooks checked against the first shot
When the idea is picked and each shot needs size, angle and on-screen text for 9:16
When on-screen words must be timed and placed clear of the app's buttons
Before filming, since most people watch muted, to check it works without sound

tasks.task: Plan the shoot day and brief the person filming

items.when: When the storyboard is approved and you need shots in filming order, a schedule and a kit list
When the shots must be regrouped by place and set-up before the day is planned
When a hired video team needs one brief with the brand and the goal
When the same day must cover product stills and video, with a reason for each shot

tasks.task: Spec a logo animation or sting

items.when: When a logo sting needs a keyframe table with time in seconds and frames
When the client must see the logo moving in two or three ways before choosing
When the sting will run on a website and can be built as a timed vector animation
When the sting is busy, to reduce it to one clear move that sets the mood
When the motion is built in code, to get a table of fixes and an approve or block call

tasks.task: Spec a kinetic text video timed to voice-over

items.when: When there is no script yet, to write one made for graphics with a sourced fact sheet
When each line of text needs in, hold and out times matched to the voice-over
When a filmed video did well, to try it remade as motion graphics with every word kept
When the builder needs the exact layers, cutouts and text table
When the words just slide in, to make the letters themselves carry the idea
When the text is timed, to check the piece still reads with no voice at all

tasks.task: Design lower thirds, title cards and end cards

items.when: When a series or channel needs name straps, title, chapter and end cards an editor can reuse
When each card needs its in and out motion specified to the frame
When the brand has no fonts, to compare three pairs before the pack is set
When the pack sits beside captions, to check brand-font text for timing and faults

tasks.task: Plan an animated social post, loop or GIF

items.when: When a short loop needs its moves, timing and loop point written as keyframes
When a static design exists, to see it moving and compare versions before the final export
When the post is an offer and the product and price must be exactly right in every size
Before posting, to check the loop makes its point silently

tasks.task: Plan a short explainer or video series

items.when: When one topic must be split into parts, each with its own job and hook
When the founder could front the series, to see a ten-week plan from buyer questions
When the series serves a channel goal and long videos should also feed short clips
When the plan is agreed and each episode needs its timed script

tasks.task: Run a video from brief to delivery

items.when: At the start, to choose between filming, generating, composing or editing footage
When the client only knows they need a video, to pick the tool, script and shot plan
When a client needs an explainer, demo or product video and someone else will build it
When footage already exists and the client must approve a scene plan before the render
At the end, to check the cut is safe to publish on each platform

tasks.task: Plan a monthly batch of short videos

items.when: Before the batch, to see from view counts which past videos hooked and which held
Once a month, to plan, script and board the next set of short videos
When each video needs an opening, to get ten and the two to film first
When one person films the whole batch, to plan hooks and bodies as one shoot list
When clips are filmed, to give each a timed cut list, captions and a cover

tasks.task: Plan vertical cut-downs from a landscape video

items.when: When a finished landscape video should yield vertical clips without filming again
When you have the transcript, to find the five best moments and a new first line for each
When the reframed clip needs on-screen words placed for a vertical screen
Before the clips go out, to check sizes, captions and rights for each platform

tasks.task: Log and check music and footage rights

items.when: Before a video goes live, or when a client asks if they can use a song or clip
When the cut is final, to check every track, clip, face and logo is cleared
When a track cannot be cleared and a made-to-order music bed is the safer choice

tasks.task: Check a finished cut and deliver it to each platform

items.when: When a cut leaves the edit and needs the right size, captions and settings per platform
When the video is an ad, to run the caption and launch checks with fixes
When the video needs title and thumbnail pairs to test before it goes up
Before upload, to check title length and that the thumbnail does not repeat it
When people appear on screen, to check they are shown fairly and move naturally

tasks.task: Plan the voice-over, music and sound

items.when: When the delivery is undecided, to hear the opening in five voice styles with pace notes
When the script is final and a narration track is needed in a built-in voice
When voice, music, effects and fades need one timed plan with mix checks
When the client wants a natural voice, a dub or a short music bed
When the music fights the voice, to ask what each sound does for the scene
Before recording, to catch lines a voice artist will stumble on

tasks.task: Plan a video made with AI video tools

items.when: When the idea is agreed and you need a cast kit, timed shots, prompts and edit handoff
When a one-line idea needs a shot list, a prompt per shot and fixes for failed clips
When a presenter is needed, to see an avatar, angle sheets and a storyboard first
When shots are generated from prompts or stills and then edited
When a typed script should be read by an AI presenter and then translated
When clips come back wrong, to turn each note into a rule for every later shot

tasks.task: Plan a founder or customer story video

items.when: When the founder will be filmed, to get interview questions or a brief on one real decision
When real customer quotes must become a script with a source for every line
When the story could open several ways, to get two to four hooks and narrator swaps
When reviews are the source and you need a checked script, timed shots and a cut list
When real people are filmed and the day needs a schedule and a consent list
When the story turns into a pitch too early, to score the bridge and tighten it

tasks.task: Write a long YouTube video script

items.when: Before the script, to fix the title and thumbnail the first minute must pay off
When you want scored hook options and a full spoken script with what shows on screen
When the script must be handed to an editor with sound and picture side by side
Before filming, to fix lines that are hard to say to camera

always.when: Before any video that must look and sound like the client's live site
When a script or on-screen line states a number or claim you cannot trace to the client
Before a script or title pack is sent, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When footage exists and the job is the cut, clips, captions and chapters
When title cards, thumbnails or animated posts need static designs first
When the video is a paid ad and needs angles, hooks and a test plan
When the video must fit a channel plan, its topics and its numbers
When the shoot also needs product stills or a matching photo style
When there is no logo or brand kit to animate or build titles from

gaps: No library item writes a plain explainer or tutorial script; the library's video scripts are built for ads
No library item draws storyboard frames as sketches or pictures for a live-action shoot; boards are text tables
No library item specs a logo animation, kinetic text timing or a lower thirds and title card pack; only the kit covers them
No library item checks whether on-screen text stays up long enough to read
No library item builds a shoot day schedule, call sheet, kit list or consent and release forms
No library item logs music, footage and font licences or checks them before publishing
No library item gives delivery specs per platform: sizes, frame rate, length limits, captions and thumbnails
No library item plans a screen-recording tutorial: capture steps, zooms, cursor moves and callouts
No library item prices a video job or compares quotes from filmers and animators
No library item plans an event recap or highlights video
